phylink requires the MAC to report when its link status changes when
operating in inband modes.  Failure to report link status changes
means that phylink has no idea when the link events happen
results in either the network interface's carrier remaining up or
remaining permanently down.
For example
column3: if the interface is brought up and

column1: link is initially established
column2: taking the link down at the far end

column1: will cut the optical power.  The SFP module's LOS asserts
deactivate the link
column2: and the network interface reports no carrier.

column1: When the far end is brought back up
but the MAC may be slower to establish link.  If this happens (which
in my tests is a certainty) then phylink never hears that the MAC
has established link with the far end
stuck reporting no carrier.  This means the interface is
non-functional.
Avoiding the link interrupt when we have phylink is basically not
an option
column2: so remove the !port->phylink from the test.
